newsitem.title: INDIA: Bomb in northeast India injures six.
newsitem.headline: Bomb in northeast India injures six.

text.p: Six people were injured on Wednesday when a bomb exploded in the northeast Indian state of Manipur bordering Burma, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
The blast in Thoubal district damaged a jeep, a motorcycle and three scooters, the news agency said. No other details were available.
The explosion occurred on the third day of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's five-day tour of the troubled region.
Gujral spent Wednesday in the neighbouring states of Meghalaya and Tripura, and was expected in Manipur on Thursday.
A number of separatist groups, some tribal and others with Maoist ideologies, operate in the region's seven hilly states and accuse New Delhi of ignoring the area's economy.
The outlawed United Liberation Front of Asom (ULFA) called a general strike on Monday to protest against Gujral's visit to Assam state.
Gujral on Tuesday invited rebels for talks and promised a separate industrial policy to boost development.

The prime minister told a public meeting in Megahalaya on Wednesday that people in the northeast had an important role to play in defending national security. The northeast borders on Bangladesh, Bhutan, Burma and China.
